items.summaryJa: レンティオでは長らくyarnとwebpackでビルドしていたが、ビルド時間と周辺プラグイン数の課題を受けてbunへ移行した。パッケージ管理は bun install に置き換え、ロックファイルは bun.lock を利用。アセットビルドは bun.build 用のプラグインを追加し、scssの処理は自作の sassPlugin、画像は Bun.Glob で列挙して仮想エントリからインポートする方式で対応。manifestは bun.build の artifacts から自作で出力、ソースマップは環境に応じて linked/external を設定。開発時は fs.watch を用いた常駐監視と別コンテナでの再ビルドで即時反映を実現し、ホットリロードは従来と異なる形になった。テストは bun test に切り替え、CIは GitHub Actions の bun setup を利用。本番ビルドはマルチステージで assets のビルドを bun の公式イメージで行い、最終イメージには public/packs のみを含める構成。CSSバンドリング時には fontawesome のUnicode文字の文字化け対策として、非ASCII文字をエスケープするプラグインを追加して対応している。

items.title: Secure internal communication between services
items.summary: Service Bindings make it easy for one Vercel service to securely call another within the same deployment. When a service declares a binding for another service, Vercel automatically injects the configured environment variable. That means user code can fetch that URL normally, while Vercel handles the internal rewrite, routing, authentication, and TLS behind the scenes. This enables multi-service applications on Vercel, like a Next.js frontend calling a FastAPI backend, while preserving service isolation and keeping routing configuration simple: In the example above, my_frontend will be able to reach the my_backend service by making a fetch() request to BACKEND_INTERNAL_URL. On the FastAPI side, my_backend exposes a normal route: Under the hood That URL points inside Vercel, not at a public address. When your code fetches it, the request travels over Vercel's internal network to the same routing layer that handles every other request to your deployment, which sends it to the target service. It never hits the public route table, and Vercel sets up the TLS trust for you, so a plain HTTPS fetch works with no certificate config. A service is only reachable if you expose it, either publicly with a rewrite route or privately with a binding. Observability Service-to-service calls also appear in observability, so you can see which bound service was called and how long the request took: Pricing Service-to-service calls are billed as Service Requests and Fast Origin Transfer . They are not billed as CDN Requests or Fast Data Transfer. See services pricing and limits for current rates.
